svg.data-ac-input-provisioning: 3600 W across three 120 VAC inputs (4800 W over four recommended), or 4000 W across two 240 VAC inputs. This is SUPPLY to be provisioned, not draw - the 4000 W is what two 240 V feeds come to, and is not a consumption figure
svg.data-psu-dc-input: -42 to -60 VDC, 20 A nominal per feed at -48 VDC

Front and rear slot N are two halves of one logical position: a DOCSIS line card in front N requires its I/O partner in rear N.","format":1,"gaps":[{"note":"The BDM2/BDM2m datasheet states \"Total Power 300 W\" in a technical specifications table headed \"BDM2/2 m with 6+12 IO Card\", whose RF connector row describes that card's six downstream and twelve upstream ports. The figure is the assembly's. A BDM position is TWO modules here - casa/bdm in a front bay and casa/io-6p12 in the paired rear bay, which is why casa/bdm already carries `pairs-with` - and no document we hold divides the 300 W between them. Writing it onto the front module would make the chassis total come out right and the answer to \"what does a BDM front module draw\" come out wrong, so neither half carries a figure and the chassis total stays a floor. The arithmetic does not settle it either way: 12 x 300 W lands on the C100G's stated 3.6 kW whether the 300 W is the pair or the front half with small rear cards. The C100G HIG corroborates the assembly reading and hedges it: Tables A-10 and A-11 both read \"Approximately 300W per BDM\" under titles scoping them to the BDM WITH its 6+12 I/O. THE LIBRARY IS CURRENTLY INCONSISTENT ABOUT THIS, ON PURPOSE AND VISIBLY. The three BDM variants carry NO power figure, for the reason above. The DQM and DCU cards added later DO carry one - DS8x8 220, DS8x96 320, DS8x192 350, US16x8 220, US16x4 150 - each with a `power-scope` provenance entry saying in the vendor's own words that the number covers the card WITH its I/O module and must not have a rear figure added to it. Both are defensible readings of the same problem: one keeps the per-module answer honest and the chassis total a floor, the other keeps the vendor's only published number reachable. They should not stay different once a pairing-scoped mechanism exists, and this is the record of which way each went and why, so that whoever unifies them is not guessing. THE THREE REAR RF I/O CARDS ADDED LATER FALL ON THE SAME SIDE OF THIS AS THE 6+12. casa/rfd, casa/rfu-16x8 and casa/ups-32x4 carry NO power figure, because Tables A-8 and A-9 give their port counts and connector types and no watts at all, and every figure Casa does publish for the slot is already the pair's - Table A-3 heads the DQM column \"Maximum consumption with I/O module\" and Table A-4 gives \"Single DCU w/ RFU I/O\" 200 W against \"Single DCU w/ RFU UPS 32x4 I/O\" 220 W for the same US16x8. Subtracting one from the other to get a rear card's share would be our arithmetic and would also be the wrong subtraction - the 20 W is the difference between two PAIRINGS, not between two I/O cards.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["casa/bdm2@1","casa/bdm2m@1","casa/bdm@1","casa/ds-8x192@1","casa/ds-8x8@1","casa/ds-8x96@1","casa/io-6p12-io2@1","casa/io-6p12-sw-io2@1","casa/io-6p12-sw@2","casa/io-6p12@2","casa/rfd@1","casa/rfu-16x8@1","casa/ups-32x4@1","casa/us-16x4@1","casa/us-16x8@1"],"wanted":"a pairable unit that can carry properties, so that a figure measured on a pair can be attached to the pair. The scope is now DATA - every card here declares `power-draw-scope: module-with-paired-io`, so a chassis sum knows not to add the rear partner and L30 catches it if one gains its own figure - but the scope says only THAT the figure covers a pair, not WHICH pair. The C100G HIG gives the same US16x8 200 W with the RFU I/O and 220 W with the RFU UPS 32x4, and the manifest can carry only one of them. Asking for \"a per-module figure\" was the wrong question: Casa states none, and one may not exist to be divided out. What is missing is the mechanism, and enough vendors doing this to design one from - Casa is the only one in the corpus.","what":"paired-module-power"},{"blocks":[],"note":"The HIG body text states \"Each fan assembly module has a maximum power consumption of 100W, totaling 300W across the three fan assemblies\". Table A-2 of the same guide gives the row \"Fan assembly (3)\" as \"330W maximum, 220W typical\". Both are about the set of three and 300 is not 330. The contract takes 100 W because it is the only figure stated PER MODULE, which is the granularity a bay occupant needs; dividing 330 by three would be our arithmetic, not the vendor's. A chassis total is therefore 30 W light against the guide's own set figure, and no per-module typical exists at all.","reason":"sources-disagree","scope":["casa/fan@1"],"wanted":"a measurement from a running chassis, a vendor erratum, or a later revision of the guide that drops one of the two figures","what":"fan-power-sources"},{"blocks":[],"note":"Casa rates a power ENTRY module in amps and volts, never in watts. Table A-1 gives \"Voltage -42 to -60VDC\" and \"Current 20A nominal per feed\", and the chassis nameplate at Figure 1-3 gives \"-48VDC, 30A per Feed (4+4 Feeds)\" - but no document states a wattage, and deriving one means choosing a point the vendor left open: two current figures across a voltage range put V x I anywhere from about 810 W to 1800 W per feed. A power entry module also does not convert or regulate; it filters and distributes what the plant feeds it, so its rating is a current-carrying limit rather than the continuous output power-output-w means. The stated volts and amps are recorded in the contract's attrs; the L27 warning stays standing as the record that the watt figure is missing.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["casa/pem@1"],"wanted":"a wattage for the C100G power entry module from Casa - a nameplate photograph of the module itself would do it, or any document that rates it in watts rather than amps","what":"power-entry-rating"}],"groups":{"fans":{"index-origin":1,"role":"service","term":"Fan module"},"front-slots":{"index-origin":1,"role":"traffic","term":"Slot"},"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Item"},"grounding":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Point"},"power":{"index-origin":1,"role":"service","term":"PEM"},"rear-slots":{"index-origin":1,"role":"traffic","term":"Slot"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"Casa Systems","maturity":"modelled","model":"C100G","name":"c100g","portfolio":{"family":"CMTS/CCAP"},"provenance":{"airflow":"Jason - air is drawn in at the rear, passes behind and through the cards, and exhausts at the FRONT bottom. So the grille below the filter is the fan EXHAUST, not an intake, and it is a coarse wire grille rather than perforation","bands":"drawing - front is air baffle above (0 to 108.1), cards, then FILTER (453.5) and the fan tray below. Rear is fan assemblies above (0 to 105.9), cards, then two power entry modules from 491.4. Fig 1-1 and Fig 1-2","captions":"the HIG has no \"Ground Strap\" text anywhere - it says ESD strap receptacle, 21 times - and no \"Cable Manager\" text either. Both were the modeller naming parts, so both have moved out of silkscreen[] (ink on the metal) into regions (author annotation), carrying the vendor word rather than the invented one. Fan L/C/R and Grounding Studs on the rear were the same species and were held back one pass for want of a rear photograph, since they sit beside PEM A/PEM B, which a rear panel plausibly does print. Owner confirmed 2026-08-25 that they are NOT printed, so they are regions too. PEM A and PEM B stay in silkscreen: they were not part of that question and nothing says they are absent from the metal","card-aspect":"NOTE - the isolated card figures (1-14, 1-15, 1-8) are drawn NARROWER than the real card. Their faceplate aspect is 13.26; the chassis front view gives 345.5 by 30.46 = 11.34, about 17 percent wider. Port positions taken from those figures are therefore used as FRACTIONS of the faceplate and stretched to this width, not as absolute geometry","card-height":"drawing - Figure 1-1 puts the card band between the slot-number strip at 18.9 percent and the FILTER band at 79.4 percent of chassis height, so 108.1 to 453.5, a 345.5 card. An earlier 440 was wrong and made the cards overrun the space above","chassis":"datasheet - Table A-1 of the C100G Hardware Installation Guide (rev 07/08/2022): 22.5in (571mm) H, 19in (482mm) W, 15.25in (386mm) D, 13RU","configurations":"datasheet - the redundancy layouts are stated per scheme in Chapter 3 (Remote PHY) and Chapter 4 (BDM)","decor-confidence":"EVERY PROJECTING DECOR ENTRY ON THIS CHASSIS NOW SAYS WHERE ITS NUMBER CAME FROM. A device's 3D was the one place in the library that could not: a component gained `confidence` on every relief feature this afternoon while a chassis went on extruding decor with nothing attached, which is the same asymmetry one level up - a projection nobody sourced looks exactly like a measured one. ALL THIRTY ARE `estimated` AND NOT ONE IS A MEASUREMENT. The branding faceplate is the owner's unaided \"sticks out almost an inch\" off the real chassis - a statement from someone holding it, which is worth more than a guess and is still not an instrument reading. The twenty-eight hook entries carry that same 24.0, so they are ONE estimate used twenty-nine times; the 2.5 plate thickness behind lift 21.5 appears in no source at all; and the air grille's 60 predates the key with its origin unrecorded. NOTE THE VOCABULARY HAS NO TOKEN FOR AN OWNER'S UNAIDED STATEMENT, which is a recurring source on this platform and sits between `estimated` and `measured`. Rather than invent one, each source says in words what it is. Worth a token if a third platform needs it.","front-face-relief":"TWO THINGS ON THIS FACE STAND PROUD AND BOTH ARE THE OWNER'S OBSERVATION, not a document: the branding faceplate across the top, and the row of fourteen cable management fingers above the slot numbers. Neither Casa guide gives a projection for anything, on any part - a search of both guides for the field names returns power, voltage, current, airflow and port counts, and no depth of anything. THE ONE NUMBER IS HIS: the top faceplate \"sticks out almost an inch\". 24.0 mm is that, and it is the only measurement behind either entry. THE FINGERS ARE HOOKS, NOT BLOCKS, and that is the owner's photograph rather than anyone's inference. working/photos/casa/c100g-front-isometric.png and its crop crop-count.png show each one as an L - a horizontal FOOT projecting forward at the base, with a thin vertical PLATE standing at the FRONT of that foot. Cables rest on the feet and are retained between the plates. A single `out` on the outline extrudes a solid from the panel, so the row rendered as fourteen cubes. Each is now TWO decor rects: the foot at full 24.0 depth, and the plate at 21.5..24.0 using the `lift` that decor gained for this. THE ONLY NEW NUMBER IS THE 2.5 PLATE THICKNESS, which is an ESTIMATE of sheet metal and is not in the photograph. THE COUNT IS FOURTEEN AND IT WAS RE-COUNTED, not inherited. A high-pass column scan of crop-count.png finds FIFTEEN objects on a pitch that widens 74 to 97 px left to right with perspective; the leftmost, read at 5x, is not a hook - it is the rail's END RETURN, square-topped and flush to the chassis side wall, and the right end carries the matching return with a captive screw through it. So the row is return + 14 hooks + return, and the fourteen already modelled are right. WHAT THE PHOTOGRAPH DOES NOT GIVE IS A DIMENSION, and it must not be read as though it did. It is a three-quarter view: every forward projection is foreshortened by an unknown factor and nothing of known size is in frame. It settles SHAPE, COUNT and ARRANGEMENT and nothing else - which is enough to turn a cube into a hook without touching a single magnitude. THE FINGERS' PROJECTION IS TIED TO THE FACEPLATE'S RATHER THAN ESTIMATED SEPARATELY. He says they stick out and gives no figure. Carrying the faceplate's 24.0 across is ONE estimate used twice, not two readings that agree - said here because fifteen decor entries now read 24.0 and that must not look like fifteen measurements. A cable finger may well project further than a bezel; nothing here says it does. Closed by a dimensioned side elevation. Figure 1-5 is NOT one - it is a schematic airflow section with no scale, and it is the only sectional view either guide has.","front-furniture":"photograph + drawing - the top is a sloped shroud carrying the casa systems mark and the model, with a row of card-guide tabs along its lower lip, then the black slot-number strip. Numbers run 0 to 13 with 6 and 7 in RED, which is how both the product photo and Fig 1-1 mark the SMM pair","protecting-slots":"SETTLED, and the manifest was half wrong. The protecting rear slots take a DIFFERENT card in each redundancy scheme, and only one of the two was modelled. In the BDM 11+1 scheme the guide lists \"Slot 5 - LC-BDM-SWITCH\" and \"Slot 8 - 6+12 SW-IO or 6+12 SW-IO2 (Slot 8 is non-redundant with 11+1 redundancy)\", which is what bdm2m-11plus1 already had. In the classic scheme Table A-2 puts an LC Switch in BOTH - its RFS row reads \"LC Switch in rear slots 5 and 8, SMM Switch in rear slots 6 and 7\" - and docsis-classic was silent on rear-8, so it inherited the bay default and quietly showed a switched I/O where the classic scheme has a switch. Its own description had said \"with LC Switch behind both\" the whole time. Both cards are now in rear-8s accepts because both are cited, and each configuration names the one its own scheme uses","rear-order":"Jason - the rear slot order is MIRRORED. Rear N connects to front N, so viewed from the back the numbering runs right to left: rear 0 sits directly behind front 0, which is on the far side when you walk round. Rear bay x is therefore FL + (13 - N) * pitch, not FL + N * pitch","rear-slots":"datasheet - C100G rear side (11+1) in Chapter 4, verbatim: slots 0-4 6+12 IO or IO2; slot 5 LC-BDM-SWITCH for BDM line module redundancy; slots 6 and 7 SMM-SW-BDM-A and -B respectively, with the guide noting that correct slot positions are indicated on the module faceplates; slot 8 6+12 SW-IO or SW-IO2, non-redundant under 11+1; slots 9-13 6+12 IO or IO2","side-faces":"drawing plus a stated absence. NO FIGURE IN THE GUIDE SHOWS THESE FOUR FACES - Figures 1-1 and 1-2 are the front and rear, 1-5 is an airflow cross-section, and 2-6 and 2-7 are rack elevations. So they are sized from Table A-1 (\"Height: 22.5 in. (571 mm), Depth: 15.25 in. (386 mm)\"; the table's 19 in / 482 mm width is the RACK face INCLUDING the mounting flanges, so the 432.95 body width the chassis block already carries is used instead), and they carry only what the guide states is on them. That is: the mounting flanges, which the guide calls integral - \"Integrated mounting flanges are included with the chassis\" - and fixes at four screws per side, since \"You must provide the eight screws that attach the CMTS to the rack\"; and the chassis label, which the guide locates precisely at \"The C100G product label is affixed to the top front side of the chassis\". The flange is integral and runs the full height at the FRONT edge, so it shows on every face that meets that edge - top, bottom, left and right - which is why the same strip appears on all four rather than being decoration invented per face. Orientation convention: top and bottom put the chassis front at y = 0, left puts it at x = 0, and right mirrors it to x = depth. NOTHING ELSE IS DRAWN ON THESE FACES, deliberately. The bottom is bare beyond the flange because the guide says nothing about it except \"grab the bottom of the chassis\" when lifting - no feet, no vents, no label. No top or bottom vents are drawn either: the guide and Jason disagree about which way the air goes (see the airflow entry), but both readings are front-to-rear or rear-to-front, and neither puts an opening on these two faces. An invented top plate would be the wrong-box outcome these four views exist to prevent","slot-compatibility":"drawing - Table A-2, \"C100G capacities\", states it directly rather than leaving it to be inferred: \"14 line card slots on front - 1 Switch and Management (SMM) module, 1 SMM redundant module, 12 DOCSIS modules (any combination of DS and US modules)\". front-6 and front-7 are the SMM pair, which the guide fixes elsewhere at \"full redundancy between chassis slots 6 and 7\"; the other twelve take the DS and US cards, and \"any combination\" is a real statement that every one of the twelve takes every DS and US card, so it is modelled as it reads. The CSC is placed by slot number in its own right - \"the CSC 8x10G can occupy up to twelve slots on the C100G platform (using slots 0-5 and 8-13 for up to 96 ports)\" - which is exactly the same twelve. Blank face plates go in any unpopulated slot, front or rear: \"Ensure that all unpopulated slots have the blank faceplate installed\". Table A-2's rear half is deliberately NOT widened - \"14 RF I/O slots on back - 0 to 4 RF I/O switch cards for DOCSIS-module redundancy in rear slots 5 and 8, remaining 10 slots available for RF I/O cards\" - so front cards stay out of rear bays, which the existing rear accepts lists already respect. Bay defaults are unchanged; this widens only what each bay is DECLARED to take","slot-pitch":"drawing - 426.6mm card region from Fig 1-1 over 14 slots = 30.47","slots":"datasheet - 14 module slots front and rear, SMM in front 6 and 7","smm-slots":"datasheet - front 6 and 7 take the SMM. Modelled with the 8x10GigE variant (Fig 1-8); the guide also lists SMM 2x10GE, SMM 300G and SMM 300Gm, which are further skins or components when needed","switch-slot-print":"drawing - a free check that PASSES, and it comes off the card rather than off the chassis. Figure 1-14 of this guide, \"BDM module, SMM Switch BDM A, B, and LC Switch BDM\", draws the two SMM Switch faceplates with their slot assignments PRINTED ON THE PLATE: A reads \"C100G Slot 6 / C40G Slot 2\" and B reads \"C100G Slot 7 / C40G Slot 3\". rear-6 accepts casa/smm-sw-bdm-a@1 and rear-7 accepts casa/smm-sw-bdm-b@1, which is what the silkscreen says. This is better evidence than the slot list it agrees with: a chassis drawing can be redrawn wrongly, but a part that names its own slot on its own face is the vendor committing twice","width":"Table A-1 quotes 19in / 482, which is the rack face INCLUDING the mounting ears. Jason confirmed from a real chassis that the ears sit outside the body and that there is only a 1/8in (3.175mm) flange either side of the cards. Working back: the card region measures 426.6 in Fig 1-1, so the BODY is 426.6 + 2x3.175 = 432.95, and the ears must protrude 24.5 each side to reach 482.
